original_test_intent: Download, activate and verify an approved NVMe M.2 firmware image on the exact intended controller/namespace, confirming the expected FW Rev change and absence of errors after the required target reset.
original_method: Before any write, bind controller and namespace through model/serial/PCI path and confirm it is non-boot and quiesced; validate owner-supplied image, checksum, compatibility, slot/action and recovery; only after explicit approval run the vendor-supported download/commit/reset sequence once; then verify the same device, expected active revision, namespaces, health, errors and service state.
manual_activity: The storage owner supplies and approves image/tool/checksum, target identity, slot/action, maintenance and recovery, explicitly authorizes each state-changing phase, and decides the final verdict from pre/post health evidence.
required_inputs: Exact M.2 controller/namespace model, serial, PCI path and device nodes
Current and expected FW revisions plus active/staged slot map
Vendor-approved image, immutable checksum, release notes and compatibility matrix
Approved nvme-cli/vendor tool and driver/kernel requirements
Boot/mount/IO ownership, quiesce and maintenance-window evidence
Backup/replacement media, stable power and vendor recovery/RMA procedure
Explicit download, activation/commit and reset authorization
safety_requirements: Never infer target identity from /dev/nvme numbering alone
Do not flash a boot, mounted, in-use, ambiguous or unsupported device
Verify image checksum, model compatibility, slot/action and vendor reset requirements before writing
Use stable power and prohibit concurrent I/O or unrelated controller reset
Capture complete outputs and exit status for each phase
Stop on any error, timeout, disappearance, identity/revision anomaly or health regression
Do not automatically retry a download, commit, reset or power action
agent_execution_scope: Perform read-only identity, current revision, mount/boot/IO and health prechecks
Validate supplied artifacts and prepare the exact proposed state-changing commands
Execute each approved write/reset phase only after current explicit owner authorization and all gates pass
Never select an image/target/slot, approve risk, retry failure or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve exact target, image/tool/checksum, expected revision, activation slot/action and reset semantics
Approve maintenance, quiesce, backup, power stability and recovery/RMA plan
Authorize state-changing phases and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED after post-flash evidence

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its generic vendor-tool statement captures package need but cannot execute or verify the source procedure and uses invalid PARTIAL classification.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After all approvals, use the vendor-supported equivalent of download and commit/activate against the verified controller or namespace path, reset only the mapped controller when required, and stop after any nonzero exit or identity change.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Source nvme list, /dev/nvme0n1 download/activation intent, action 1, slot 2, /dev/nvme0 reset, FW Rev comparison, Config-Check and 20/20-minute values remain; literal paths and parameters require owner validation rather than silent replacement.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an immutable target-and-image manifest, staged prechecks, one authorized download/commit/reset path and a full pre/post identity/health diff.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds destructive-action authorization, artifact/target integrity and recovery without changing the requested firmware-update coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A revision change alone does not prove correct target, data availability, namespace integrity, health or service recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Incorrect or interrupted firmware can brick the controller or lose data/service; recovery may require vendor tooling or replacement.

project_override_considerations: If the vendor requires a different command, device node, slot or power cycle, the owner must approve the exact equivalent and document preserved download/activation/reset/version coverage before use.
expected_evidence: Owner approvals, maintenance/quiesce record, target model/serial/PCI/controller/namespace identity and boot/mount/IO status
Image/tool/release-note identity, checksums, compatibility and expected revision/slot/action
Complete download/commit/reset outputs and exit codes with timestamps
Same-device post-flash active revision, namespace, health/SMART/error, kernel and service evidence
No-retry audit, any recovery evidence and owner PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source hard-codes namespace/controller paths, action and slot without target/image/compatibility or recovery data and accepts only a version change/no error. DeepSeek uses an invalid PARTIAL classification. The same code also labels an unrelated row-2203 USB testcase.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The static review is complete; execution is gated by supplyable package, identity, maintenance, recovery and explicit approval rather than structurally impossible.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2041 variant d6167928957fd81c of shared code Wistron-HW-00484-V002: approve the exact M.2 model/serial/controller/namespace target, vendor image/tool/checksum and expected FW revision; validate download/commit action 1 slot 2 and reset semantics, boot/quiesce/maintenance/power/recovery gates and post-flash integrity criteria; keep row 2203 USB2/3 Function Check strictly separate.

review_improvement: Converts an invalid PARTIAL label into the approved package/confirmation class, makes destructive gates and no-retry behavior explicit, and extends acceptance from version text to same-device health and service integrity.
independent_technical_reasoning: Firmware download, activation and controller reset are irreversible-risk operations whose safety depends on exact physical identity and image compatibility, not a volatile /dev path. Namespace and controller nodes may differ legitimately, but their mapping must be proven before reset. A changed FW Rev can coexist with a wrong target or degraded namespaces, so post-flash identity and health checks are mandatory and any failure must halt rather than trigger an automatic retry.
